source.title: ConViT: improving vision transformers with soft convolutional inductive biases
source.authors: Stéphane d'Ascoli; Hugo Touvron; Matthew L. Leavitt; Ari S. Morcos; G. Biroli; Levent Sagun

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendices is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how soft convolutional positional bias and related architectural conditions affect image-classification test accuracy and internal attention locality; this is an extension of the listed architecture-bias findings to vision transformers.
record.gate_note: Reports test accuracy comparisons and internal locality measurements relevant to V3. It does not report random-label memorization, width sweeps past interpolation, train-test error gaps, or sharpness-gap comparisons. Cited results from prior work are not extracted as rows. Accuracy ablations are reported on full or subsampled ImageNet, and one set on the first 100 ImageNet classes; the study does not provide corresponding training errors.
record.test_reason: The study tests convolutional initialization and positional attention in vision transformers, not V3's comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks. Its accuracy, locality and masking results do not test any other listed version. Discussion of CNN-versus-FCN findings cites earlier work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that convolutional initialization with gated positional attention improves vision-transformer trainability and sample efficiency while preserving flexibility to use content attention. These conclusions concern ConViT and DeiT, not a demonstrated CNN-versus-FCN advantage.
record.recipe_differences: Compares ViT/DeiT and a new GPSA-based ConViT architecture using positional gating and convolutional initialization; evaluates image-classification accuracy and internal attention locality, not the original CNN-versus-FCN comparison or train-test gap measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with GPSA layer count, locality strength, gating, convolutional initialization, dataset size, and whether attention layers are frozen; attention locality/gating behavior also varies by layer and model size. Distillation changes DeiT nonlocality.

fits_no_version.finding: ConViT improves transformer classification accuracy and sample efficiency: Table 1 reports 73.1 versus 72.2 for tiny models; Table 2 reports 59.6 versus 48.0 for small models at 10% ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Soft convolutional positional biases can improve vision-transformer accuracy and sample efficiency relative to DeiT under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Transformer accuracy depends on positional-attention parameterization, initialization, trainability and data availability. Table 3 reports 82.2 for the full model versus 79.1 for DeiT, while frozen random GPSA reaches 73.7. Vanilla PSA eventually falls below DeiT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of convolutional initialization in vision transformers depend on how positional and content attention are combined and trained.

fits_no_version.finding: DeiT attention initially becomes more local; ConViT escapes its initially local configuration while retaining positional attention in some lower-layer heads. Distillation makes DeiT attention more local.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision-transformer attention locality evolves with training, layer depth, initialization and distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: Masking absolute positional embeddings reduces DeiT-Ti accuracy from 72.2 to 38.3 and ConViT-Ti from 73.1 to 67.1. Masking content attention throughout ConViT's GPSA layers reduces accuracy to 1.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ConViT relies less than DeiT on absolute positional embeddings, but strongly depends on content attention.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 139 (2021)
record.problems: No train-error results or train-test gap measurements; no random-label task; no direct CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison. Most comparisons report accuracy without uncertainty. Some values are figure-only. The prose and Table 2 differ for 10% ImageNet accuracy (59.5/46.5 in prose versus 59.6/48.0 in table), and the full-data ablation prose's stated gains do not map cleanly to Table 3 conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. Several draft entries were consolidated to avoid retaining unsupported or duplicative values: the prose's 59.5/46.5 sample-efficiency figures are acknowledged in the notes alongside Table 2, and figure-only locality-strength accuracy values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
All parts: CNN-versus-FCN generalization, the contribution of local connectivity to that comparison, learned sparse local connections in FCNs, and initialization of FCNs from trained CNNs.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Joint learning-rate and batch-size changes for larger models do not isolate this effect.
Dropout effects, underfitting from excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized examples, with random-removal controls and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No tools or external sources used. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions because their measures or model comparisons fall outside those versions. This does not dispute the reported transformer effects. The apparent Table 3 gain-mapping ambiguity is resolvable from its explicit row references; the Table 2 numerical discrepancy and Table 3 versus Figure 12 dataset inconsistency remain.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label train-versus-test generalization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.

Does not compare standard convolutional networks directly against fully connected networks trained from scratch, nor test learned sparse local connections or convolution-initialized fully connected networks. It compares DeiT and ConViT transformer architectures and their positional-bias ablations.
No dropout or weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining experiment.

rows.subject: DeiT-Ti
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet-1k classification with the DeiT recipe; reported as the same-size and same-flops comparator to ConViT-Ti.
rows.note: Comparator for the architectural-bias accuracy result; the study does not report training error or a fully connected network here.
rows.check: Transformer comparator, not a CNN-versus-FCN comparison. Table 1 attributes this DeiT-Ti result to Touvron et al.; flag as a cited baseline rather than this study's own training result.

rows.subject: ConViT-Ti
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet-1k classification using the ConViT with GPSA layers and convolutional initialization.
rows.note: ConViT exceeds its same-size DeiT comparator by 0.9 percentage points; this is a transformer comparison, not a direct CNN-versus-FCN test.
rows.check: The 73.1 versus 72.2 comparison measures ConViT versus DeiT, outside V3's named architectures; a partial V3 effect cannot be inferred.

rows.subject: DeiT-Ti
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet-1k classification on 10% of each class's training images, with epoch count increased inversely to the fraction.
rows.value: 46.5% (described in text; table reports 47.8 for ConViT-S versus 48.0 for DeiT-S at 10%)
rows.locator: Sample efficiency of the ConViT; Table 2 and text
rows.note: The text's 46.5% value is a DeiT-S comparison, not DeiT-Ti; therefore this row's subject label would be unsupported. Excluded from row-level evidence; see R4 for the clearly attributed Table 2 comparison.
rows.check: Remove this unsupported subject assignment. The prose's 46.5 refers to DeiT-S, not DeiT-Ti, and conflicts with Table 2's 48.0. It is an alternative report of the R4 comparison, not a separate experiment.

rows.subject: DeiT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained with original DeiT hyperparameters; epochs multiplied by 1/f
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet-1k classification using a 10% per-class training subset.
rows.locator: Table 2; Sample efficiency of the ConViT
rows.note: The cited text later says 46.5% for the DeiT counterpart, while Table 2 gives 48.0; retain the tabulated value and note the discrepancy.
rows.check: Table 2 reports DeiT-S accuracy of 48.0 at 10% training data; prose reports 46.5. Neither tests a listed version.

rows.subject: ConViT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained with original DeiT hyperparameters; epochs multiplied by 1/f
rows.operation_detail: ImageNet-1k classification using a 10% per-class training subset.
rows.locator: Table 2; Sample efficiency of the ConViT
rows.note: Table 2 reports 59.6; the prose reports 59.5 for the ConViT-S and 46.5 for its DeiT counterpart.
rows.check: The Table 2 comparison is correctly 59.6 versus 48.0, but compares transformers rather than the systems named in V3.

rows.subject: DeiT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification on the first 100 ImageNet classes, using the matched + model setup.
rows.note: Control architecture for ConViT-S+ ablations.
rows.check: Transformer baseline outside V3. The first-100-classes condition conflicts with Table 3's full-ImageNet caption and main-text description; Figure 12 describes a first-100-classes experiment with the same values.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with 10 GPSA layers, convolutional initialization and trainable positional gating.
rows.note: Authors report the full ConViT-S+ result.
rows.check: Transformer ablation outside V3. Table 3 identifies full ImageNet, whereas Figure 12 describes the same values on the first 100 classes. Flag this source inconsistency; also duplicates R19.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with gating parameters frozen to zero and convolutional initialization retained.
rows.note: Ablation condition tests positional gating's contribution.
rows.check: Transformer ablation outside V3. Table 3 identifies full ImageNet, conflicting with the recorded first-100-classes condition and Figure 12. Frozen lambda=0 means equal positional and content weights, not elimination of positional attention.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with convolutional initialization removed; GPSA and trainable gating retained.
rows.note: Ablation condition tests the contribution of convolutional initialization.
rows.check: Transformer ablation outside V3. Table 3 identifies full ImageNet, conflicting with the recorded first-100-classes condition and Figure 12.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with gating and convolutional initialization removed; GPSA retained.
rows.note: The table's row d freezes gating to zero and removes convolutional initialization; the condition is therefore gating frozen, not trainable.
rows.check: Table 3 row d freezes gating to lambda=0 and removes convolutional initialization; change trainable gating to frozen. Dataset descriptions conflict between Table 3 and Figure 12. Outside V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with all GPSA layers frozen after convolutional initialization.
rows.note: Frozen convolution-initialized GPSA falls 0.5 points below the DeiT-S+ comparator; authors call it almost equalling DeiT.
rows.check: Frozen transformer attention is outside V3; the 78.6 versus 79.1 result is not a partial V3 effect. Dataset descriptions conflict between Table 3 and Figure 12.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification with GPSA layers frozen after random initialization.
rows.note: Randomly initialized frozen GPSA is 5.4 points below DeiT-S+.
rows.check: Random frozen transformer attention is outside V3; its lower accuracy cannot reverse V3. Dataset descriptions conflict between Table 3 and Figure 12.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+

rows.operation_detail: Image classification on 10% of ImageNet training data using the full ConViT-S+ recipe.

rows.check: Use Table 3's matched DeiT-S+ baseline of 47.8, not DeiT-S in Table 2, whose 10% value is 48.0. Remove the first-100-classes stage description: Table 3 describes 10% of ImageNet. Outside V3.

rows.operation_detail: Image classification on 10% of ImageNet training data with gating frozen to zero; convolutional initialization retained.

rows.operation_detail: Image classification on 10% of ImageNet training data with convolutional initialization removed; GPSA and trainable gating retained.

rows.operation_detail: Image classification on 10% of ImageNet training data with gating frozen and convolutional initialization removed.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Image classification on 10% of ImageNet training data with GPSA layers frozen after random initialization.
rows.note: Randomly initialized frozen GPSA falls below the DeiT-S comparator.
rows.check: Use Table 3's DeiT-S+ baseline of 47.8. Remove the first-100-classes stage description; this column concerns 10% ImageNet. Lower transformer accuracy does not reverse V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on full ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Training with positional and content attention as in the full model.
rows.note: Text states the gains from full ImageNet ablations: GPSA alone +2.5, convolutional initialization +2.9, gating with initialization +3.1 versus DeiT.
rows.check: Duplicates R7's Table 3 result; consolidate and retain the Table 3 versus Figure 12 dataset inconsistency. Outside V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+ without gating
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: GPSA with convolutional initialization, but without positional gating.
rows.measure: Top-1 accuracy difference relative to DeiT
rows.note: The specific absolute accuracy is not stated in this passage.
rows.check: The +2.5 gain refers to Table 3 row d: gating frozen and convolutional initialization absent, yielding 81.6 versus 79.1. The recorded initialization condition is wrong. Duplicate of R10, outside V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+ without convolutional initialization
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: GPSA with trainable gating but without convolutional initialization.
rows.measure: Top-1 accuracy difference relative to DeiT
rows.note: Passage says initialization slightly increases the GPSA-only benefit; condition/result mapping is ambiguous relative to Table 3, so preserve the stated comparison.
rows.check: The +2.9 gain refers to Table 3 row b: convolutional initialization retained and gating frozen, yielding 82.0 versus 79.1. Both recorded conditions are wrong. Duplicate of R8, outside V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: GPSA with both gating and convolutional initialization.
rows.measure: Top-1 accuracy difference relative to DeiT
rows.note: Authors describe the gating benefit as present with convolutional initialization.
rows.check: The +3.1 gain is the same Table 3 comparison as R7 and R19, not an independent result. Outside V3.

rows.subject: ConViT-B with vanilla PSA
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Convolutional initialization with GPSA layers replaced by vanilla PSA, so content and positional terms share the standard PSA parameterization.
rows.value: initial advantage, then DeiT catches up and surpasses ConViT late in training; exact values figure only
rows.note: Appendix says vanilla PSA stays in the convolutional configuration and late performance is surpassed by DeiT.
rows.check: Vanilla-PSA ConViT versus DeiT tests a transformer parameterization; its late-training disadvantage does not reverse V3.

rows.subject: DeiT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention nonlocality over training, averaged over a batch of 1024 images.
rows.value: falls early in all layers; later remains low in lower layers and rises in upper layers
rows.note: Internal attention locality is a measured property, not the train-test generalization gap named in V7.
rows.check: Attention nonlocality does not measure CNN-versus-FCN generalization or magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps.

rows.subject: ConViT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured attention nonlocality over training, averaged over a batch of 1024 images.
rows.value: grows in all GPSA layers during training; final nonlocality remains below DeiT
rows.note: Authors describe escape from locality while retaining some initialization effect.
rows.check: Attention nonlocality does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: ConViT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean positional gating over attention heads during training.
rows.value: decreases during training; reaches 0 in layers 6–10, while some heads in layers 1–5 retain high values
rows.note: The metric tracks use of positional information, not train-test gap.
rows.check: Positional gating is an internal attention measure, not a listed generalization effect.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Varied locality strength and the number of GPSA layers.
rows.note: Text says final accuracy increases with both locality strength and number of GPSA layers.
rows.check: Locality-strength and GPSA-layer ablations concern transformers, outside V3. The main text calls the model ConViT-S while Figure 8 calls it ConViT-S+; flag the attribution inconsistency.

rows.subject: ConViT-S+
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch; 300 epochs on first 100 ImageNet classes
rows.operation_detail: Varied number of GPSA layers and measured accuracy across training epochs.
rows.value: using 9 GPSA layers almost doubles test accuracy after 20 epochs
rows.note: Authors attribute early training boost to convolutional initialization.
rows.check: The early-training accuracy benefit concerns GPSA layers in a transformer, outside V3; it is not a width or batch-size experiment.

rows.subject: DeiT-S
rows.stage_stated: trained for 300 epochs on ImageNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared attention nonlocality with and without hard distillation from a RegNetY-16GF teacher.
rows.value: nonlocality rises less at late times; final states are more local
rows.note: Internal locality measure; not a generalization-gap metric.
rows.check: Distillation's effect on attention nonlocality does not measure any listed version.

rows.operation_detail: Masked absolute positional embeddings at test time.
rows.note: Masking positional embeddings severely lowers DeiT-Ti accuracy.
rows.check: Test-time positional-embedding masking measures transformer dependence on positional information, not a reversal of V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet classification, full ConViT versus same-size DeiT; full and 10% training data
reader_labels.reason: ConViT improves reported test accuracy over matched DeiT comparators in these settings (R2, R5, R7, R13). This supports an architectural-bias advantage within this transformer comparison, not the version's direct CNN-versus-FCN wording.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ConViT ablations on full and 10% ImageNet; first 100 ImageNet classes
reader_labels.reason: The result depends on the combination of GPSA, gating and convolutional initialization; freezing or randomizing attention changes accuracy, and vanilla PSA is eventually surpassed by DeiT (R8-R12, R14-R23).
